### Gage

Station and peak-flow record.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| USGS station number | 03606500 |
| Station name | Big Sandy River at Bruceton, TN |
| Drainage area (square miles) | 205 |
| Annual peaks | 44 |
| Water years | 1930 to 1973 |
| Largest peak (cfs) | 17,000 (water year 1935) |
| Smallest peak (cfs) | 1,200 (water year 1941) |
| Regulation screen | unknown: Non-ref; below storage and impervious thresholds (GAGES-II 2011-09-30) |

The annual peaks were fitted with a log-Pearson Type III distribution following Bulletin 17C (England and others, 2019): the Expected Moments Algorithm (EMA) for the moments and the Multiple Grubbs-Beck Test (MGBT) for potentially influential low floods. The computation was made with flowfreq {version}. The station skew was weighted with a regional skew of -0.500 (standard error 0.550), supplied by the analyst without a citation. MGBT identified no potentially influential low floods.

### Transposed from the gage

Flood quantiles at the ungaged site were transposed from the donor gage, USGS 03606500 Big Sandy River at Bruceton, TN, by the drainage-area ratio method: the gage's quantile at each annual exceedance probability, multiplied by the ratio of the site's drainage area to the gage's raised to the drainage-area exponent of a regional regression at that probability. The exponents are from Example and Author (2020). No distribution was fitted at the site, so there are no moments to report there. The computation was made with flowfreq {version}.

- Donor: USGS 03606500, 205.0 sq mi
- Target: ungaged target, 150.0 sq mi
- Area ratio: 0.7317
- Exponent source: Example, A.B., and Author, C.D., 2020, A made-up report for the tests, table 1.
- Region: Region 1
- Statistic: flood frequency
- Interpolation: linear (in normal-deviate space); extrapolation: clamp

Flood quantiles transposed from the gage by the drainage-area ratio.

| Annual exceedance probability (percent) | Donor flow (cfs) | Drainage-area exponent | Factor applied | Transposed flow (cfs) | Lower 90-percent limit (cfs) | Upper 90-percent limit (cfs) | Exponent basis |

| 2 | 15,801 | 0.630 | 0.8212 | 12,977 | 10,403 | 18,315 | interpolated |
| 1 | 18,069 | 0.620 | 0.8239 | 14,888 | 11,539 | 22,339 | published |
| 0.5 | 20,359 | 0.620 | 0.8239 | 16,774 | 12,526 | 26,815 | extrapolated |
| 0.2 | 23,424 | 0.620 | 0.8239 | 19,300 | 13,682 | 33,651 | extrapolated |

#### Caveats

- **8 of 14 quantiles use an extrapolated exponent**, at AEP 0.995, 0.99, 0.95, 0.9, 0.8, 0.67, 0.005, 0.002. These fall outside the range the cited regression publishes, so their exponent is an assumption of this analysis rather than a published value.
- **Regulation was not checked**: no regulation status was supplied for both donor and target. A regulated donor transfers its regulation.
- Confidence limits are the donor's, scaled by the same factor. That is first order and understates the true uncertainty: it treats the transposition as exact and carries none of the regression's own error.

### Regional regression

blocks.text: The flood quantiles at the site were estimated by 2 methods, set side by side below at the annual exceedance probabilities all of them give. blocks.text: Cautions on Urban: SIR 2025-5104 (Wagner and Ladd, 2026) is an urban set fitted to gages in six southeastern states, 20 of 136 in Tennessee. It is not valid in the Middle Atlantic or Southern Coastal Plain Level 3 ecoregions or for regulated or tidal streams; its accuracy is not known outside the study area, which is six ecoregions and had no urban gage in the Mississippi Alluvial Plain, Central Appalachians or Blue Ridge (pp. 5, 12). Nothing here checks which ecoregion the basin is in. L3_PIEDMNT and L3_RDGVLY are percent of the basin, 0 to 100, not fractions. At a gage used to develop the equations the report calls weighting them with the at-site estimate inappropriate, because the two are not independent (p. 13).
